subject.title: [Feature]: Include interaction metadata in Discord button callbacks

question: Should generic Discord component clicks expose a new typed agent-visible interaction metadata envelope, and which fields should be public instead of plugin-only?
rationale: The change would expand public inbound context and expose Discord identifiers and callback data, so maintainers need to choose the schema, compatibility shape, and trust boundary before implementation.

options.title: Add Typed Agent Metadata
options.body: Expose a documented minimal envelope with action kind, originating message id, safe callback/custom data, label/value details, and clicker identity, backed by Discord plugin tests.

options.title: Keep Metadata Plugin-Only
options.body: Leave rich interaction fields on plugin interactive handlers and document generic callbacks as text-only fallback messages.

options.title: Start With Sender And Message
options.body: Expose only clicker and originating message ids first, deferring callback payload semantics to a broader inbound metadata contract.

recommendation.title: Add Typed Agent Metadata
recommendation.body: Expose a documented minimal envelope with action kind, originating message id, safe callback/custom data, label/value details, and clicker identity, backed by Discord plugin tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The active generic callback dispatch lines are currently owned by recent Discord monitor work, and this decision crosses the same Discord/plugin boundary.
